topic: Adversarial cross-surface review of the Aug-12-2026 eclipse GEOMETRIC verdict before decider integration
scope: Reviewed 4 published surfaces (docs/eclipse-2026/index.html post-event verdict; docs/index.html hero badge id=ds-thesis-verdict-badge + 2026-08-13 Latest-Findings item; data/sections.json part4 §4.2.7 post-event callout + §4.2.6 magnetic revisit clause) against the FROZEN source of truth predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json (OTS-anchored 2026-05-02, rev2) and the analyst commission EXP-COMMISSION-eclipse-2026-08-12-geometric-verdict-1786644219.
our_argument_summary: The Aug-12-2026 total solar eclipse geometrically falsifies the dome and corroborates standard physics. Dome's own pinned V51.1 parameters (h_Sun=5,733 km, h_Moon=2,534 km) force a 1.317 km totality strip (predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json:B2-G-001) lasting ~0.9-7 s (B2-G-003); observation delivered a ~294 km path (B1-G-001) lasting 138.2 s / 2m18s (B1-G-002) — a ~223x width gap and an 8-138x duration gap. 0 of the dome's own 9 named stations fall inside the dome-forced ~85 km penumbra band (B2-G-004). OBS-D-01 fires; OBS-S-01 does not. The magnetic bucket is deliberately left open until the +30d INTERMAGNET window (~2026-09-11).

holes_found.description: The main-page Latest-Findings item (docs/index.html ~line 532) LEADS with an uncited satellite-imaging claim: headline 'Pre-Registered Dome Eclipse Prediction Falsified — Satellites Imaged the Shadow the Dome Said Couldn't Exist,' and body asserts as fact that 'geostationary and deep-space satellites (Meteosat, GOES, DSCOVR/EPIC) ... recorded a ~294-km path.' No citation or link to any satellite frame appears on ANY published surface, and no verified primary frame is embedded yet (fast-follow slot still open). The claim is TRUE and sourced in the analyst commission (EUMETSAT Meteosat-12 FCI image-of-week; Forbes 2026-08-13 photo essay; DSCOVR joint imaging) — so this is not fabrication — but for the marquee adversary-facing claim the review's own citation rigor is not met: elsewhere every figure carries a source, and the frozen file models this. A defender cannot refute the claim but can fairly say 'you assert satellites imaged it and link nothing.' The load-bearing argument does NOT depend on the image: the eclipse sub-page explicitly states 'You did not need a satellite to see this fail: two minutes of totality, observed from inhabited ground across Iceland and northern Spain, already refutes a one-second, one-kilometre shadow' — that sentence carries the verdict alone. So the fix is citation, not softening the verdict.
holes_found.recommendation: Add the EUMETSAT Meteosat-12 image-of-week URL and/or the Forbes photo-essay URL (both already present in EXP-COMMISSION-eclipse-2026-08-12-geometric-verdict) inline to the satellite sentences on BOTH the sub-page and the Latest-Findings item; OR, until a primary public-domain frame is embedded, re-lead the Latest-Findings headline with the ground-totality fact ('Two minutes of totality refute a one-second dome shadow') and demote the satellite line to a cited supporting clause.

holes_found.description: The duration ratio label '8–138×' is not reconstructable from the numbers shown in its own row on the eclipse sub-page cmp table. That row displays dome '~0.9 s (≤7 s)' and observed '2 m 18 s (138.2 s)'. From those two values a reader computes 138.2/0.9 ≈ 154× and 138.2/7 ≈ 20× — i.e. a ~20–154× band, not 8–138×. The 8× lower bound requires the ~59 s near-limit (Reykjavik) observed minimum, which appears nowhere on the page; the 138× upper bound conservatively rounds 154× down and coincidentally equals the 138 s figure. Not an overclaim (the upper bound is stated conservatively) and not a factual error, but the band mixes an observed-minimum that isn't displayed, so it reads as unsourced arithmetic to a careful reader.
holes_found.recommendation: Show observed duration as a range in the cmp table — e.g. '59–138 s (near-limit edge to central-line max)' — so both the 8× and 138× bounds trace directly; or add a one-line footnote deriving 8× = 59 s/7 s and 138× ≈ 138 s/~1 s.

holes_found.description: Cross-surface duration-multiplier inconsistency. The eclipse sub-page and the main-page Latest-Findings item both state the duration gap as '8–138×'. But data/sections.json §4.2.7 body (which also renders into docs/index.html) expresses the SAME duration shortfall as '~20×' / '45×' (and, under other assumed orbital speeds, ~19× / ~32× / ~97×). The WIDTH multiplier (223×) is uniform across every surface; only the DURATION multiplier varies. The values are not contradictory (each is a valid gap under a specific speed-bound choice), but a reader moving between the Latest-Findings blurb (8–138×) and §4.2.7 body (~20–45×) on the same main page sees different duration numbers for the same claim.
holes_found.recommendation: Harmonize: either add the 8–138× band (frozen B2-G-003 bounds 0.9–7 s vs observed 59–138 s) to §4.2.7's post-event callout so the main page tells one duration story, or add a bridging note in §4.2.7 explaining that the post-event framing widens the pre-event 20–45× estimate now that near-limit observed durations (59 s) are available.

holes_found.description: Predicted-vs-observed conflation in the sub-page comparison table. The column header reads 'Standard physics predicted — and the eclipse delivered' over the value '294 km', but 294 km is the NASA/frozen PREDICTED value (B1-G-001); the eclipse DELIVERED a satellite-measured ~290 km umbra (Meteosat-12, per the commission), which is consistent with 294 km inside the frozen OBS-D-01 ±20 km tolerance. Implying 294 km was the measured value invites a 'you said 294 but satellites measured 290' nitpick. The verdict is unaffected (290 is within 294±20).
holes_found.recommendation: Distinguish predicted from observed in the table or a footnote — e.g. '294 km predicted (B1-G-001); ~290 km observed, within the pre-registered ±20 km tolerance' — keeping 294 km as the registered figure while not presenting it as the measurement.

Download link (downloads/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json + .ots), the check-it-yourself NASA links, and the eclipse-geometry-comparison.svg asset all resolve to present files in the clone.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome's underlying arithmetic is internally consistent, and our review says so rather than strawmanning it: given the dome's own h_Sun=5,733 km and h_Moon=2,534 km with NASA's real angular semi-diameters, the parallel-ray occultation math genuinely yields a 1.317 km umbral disc and a sub-second-to-~7 s single-station totality (predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json:B2-G-001, B2-G-003). This is a correct derivation from the dome's premises, not a computational error we introduced.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Being internally consistent is exactly what makes the dome falsifiable here: the 223x width gap and 8-138x duration gap are the empirical falsification, not an interpretation dispute. The dome's own 9-station list (predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json:B2-G-004, 0/9 inside the dome-forced band) only makes sense on the globe path it argues against — so the internal consistency of the geometry converts directly into the model's defeat once real observation lands.

cross_surface_consistency: Width multiplier 223× uniform across badge, Latest-Findings, §4.2.7 callout, sub-page. Provenance (2026-05-02, ~102 days, c3b9f56/V51.1) uniform. Magnetic-open (+30d ~2026-09-11) uniform. The only cross-surface wrinkles are the duration-multiplier variance (hole #3) and the uncited satellite claim (hole #1).
summary_for_decider: Geometric verdict is SOUND — dome falsified / standard corroborated, every frozen claim-ID number traces exactly, provenance and magnetic-open integrity are clean, tone stayed on data. current_verdict_holds=true. Four fixes, none blocking the verdict: (1) MODERATE — add a citation (EUMETSAT/Forbes, already in the commission) to the uncited satellite-imaging claim that LEADS the Latest-Findings headline, or re-lead with the ground-totality fact until a primary frame is embedded; the load-bearing ground argument already carries the verdict without any image. (2) MINOR — the '8–138×' duration band isn't reconstructable from the sub-page table's own row (shows 138.2 s vs ~0.9 s → ~20–154×); show observed duration as a 59–138 s range or footnote it. (3) MINOR — §4.2.7 body says ~20–45× for the same duration gap the sub-page/Latest-Findings call 8–138×; harmonize. (4) MINOR — sub-page table labels 294 km as both 'predicted' and 'delivered'; observation was ~290 km within the ±20 km tolerance. Recommend the decider apply (1) as a patch before this hardens, and batch (2)-(4) as minor edits. Do NOT touch the frozen file or the magnetic bucket.
